stat_summary: Around 35% of women are 'super-tasters', who are born with more taste buds and perceive tastes, especially bitterness, more intensely, compared with about 15% of men, according to research led by Professor Linda Bartoshuk at Yale University. Overall, roughly a quarter of people are non-tasters, half are average tasters and a quarter are super-tasters.
stat_source_title: Tongue test identifies 'super-tasters', BBC News (2003), reporting Yale University research led by Professor Linda Bartoshuk

male.headline: The Last Sprout Brigade: Only 15 Per Cent of Men Are Super-Tasters, and They've Been Finishing Everyone's Leftovers Ever Since
male.standfirst: Science has finally explained why it is always him eating the burnt roastie, the 2019 chutney and your sprouts, and frankly he would like a medal.
male.image_caption: Keith, 58, receives his fourth donated sprout of the afternoon.
body_paragraphs: Research from Yale University has confirmed what every British dad hovering over the roasting tin already suspected: just 15 per cent of men are 'super-tasters', against around 35 per cent of women. Super-tasters experience flavours, especially bitter ones, far more intensely. Everybody else, it turns out, is simply getting on with it.

This means the average man is biologically built for the jobs nobody else will touch: the black-edged roast potato, the coffee from the office machine, the jar of chutney that has lived in the fridge door since a cousin's wedding. He is not a man with no taste. He is the household's entire food-waste strategy.

“Every Christmas there's a little procession of plates coming my way,” said Keith, 58, from Kettering. “Three sprouts from Mum, four from the kids, one parsnip with a bite out of it. I'm not a guest, I'm a bin with a paper hat on.”

Worse, his sturdy, low-drama tongue is routinely mocked. Partners say he 'would eat cardboard', and one man at a barbecue in Rugby was reportedly told he had 'the palate of a Labrador'. Nobody says that about the people who sent the risotto back.

Campaigners from Men Against Wasting Scraps (MAWS) are demanding that finishing the last sprout be formally recognised as a civic duty, with finishers entitled to first pick of the Quality Street and the good end of the sofa for the King's Speech.
Until then he will keep clearing the plates, one bitter mouthful at a time, while everyone else calls it greed.
male.pull_quote: I'm not a guest, I'm a bin with a paper hat on.

female.headline: Not Fussy, Just Fully Equipped: Women Are More Than Twice as Likely to Be Super-Tasters, and Nobody Believes Her About the Sprouts
female.standfirst: For millions of British women Christmas dinner is less a festive treat than a bitter-flavoured ambush, yet she is still being called picky by a man who once ate a Scotch egg he found in the car.
female.image_caption: Joanne, 41, confronts the sprout she was told to 'just try'.
body_paragraphs: Around 35 per cent of women are 'super-tasters', according to Yale research, compared with just 15 per cent of men. Super-tasters are born with more taste buds and perceive tastes, bitterness above all, more intensely, which means that for a third of British women a Brussels sprout is not a vegetable. It is an incident.
“I said the coffee tasted like a burnt shed and he said I was being dramatic,” said Joanne, 41, from Stockport. “I'm not dramatic. I've got more equipment. He's running on factory settings.”

Yet the word 'fussy' continues to be hurled across dinner tables nationwide, usually by someone who cannot tell own-brand cola from the real thing and once described a £4 Merlot as 'grand'. A woman who sends back a stewed tea is not being difficult. She is reporting accurate data.

Campaigners are calling for a Sprout Exemption Certificate, entitling every super-taster to a sprout-free plate at Christmas without having to explain herself to an uncle, and for the phrase 'just try one' to be banned from all tables until the new year.
Until then she will smile politely, cut the sprout into eight pieces and hide them under the turkey, like generations of under-believed women before her.
female.pull_quote: I'm not dramatic. I've got more equipment. He's running on factory settings.
